name: Terreulactone C
summary: The route employs a highly convergent and biomimetic strategy to assemble the complex polycyclic target. The key feature is a Lewis acid-catalyzed polyene cyclization that rapidly constructs the highly substituted decalin core from an acyclic terpene precursor, directly addressing the user constraint. Subsequent steps logically elaborate the core by appending a coumarin moiety, forming the pyran ring via dehydrative etherification, and finally installing the 4-methoxyphenyl group via a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling.

branch_points.comment: Suzuki coupling joining the 4-methoxyphenyl ring to the core.
Alkylation joining the coumarin moiety to the decalin core.
Enolate alkylation joining the allylic bromide and the dione to form the acyclic precursor.

stereo_comment: The route relies heavily on substrate control in highly congested environments. The polyene cyclization and the dehydrative etherification carry significant risks of forming undesired diastereomers.

handover.justification: Mol H is a relatively simple acyclic terpene-like precursor that can be easily assembled from standard geranyl/farnesyl building blocks using established enolate alkylation and cross-coupling methods. A template-based tool can easily handle its synthesis.

top_risks.risk: The biomimetic polyene cyclization (Step 6) may suffer from low yield or incorrect stereochemistry due to competing elimination pathways.
top_risks.mitigation: Extensive screening of Lewis acids, temperatures, and solvents to optimize the cascade and trap the intermediate carbocation efficiently.

top_risks.risk: Alkylation of 4-hydroxycoumarin (Step 4) may favor O-alkylation over the desired C-alkylation.
top_risks.mitigation: Use specific Lewis acids (e.g., Sc(OTf)3) or water-based conditions known to favor C-alkylation of 4-hydroxycoumarins.

top_risks.risk: Dehydrative etherification (Step 2) may lead to epimerization at the tertiary alcohol, giving a mixture of diastereomers.
top_risks.mitigation: Carefully control reaction time and acidity, or explore alternative milder cyclization conditions to ensure thermodynamic control favors the desired epimer.

building_blocks.flag: May require custom synthesis from geraniol derivatives.
3,3-dimethylpentane-2,4-dione is commercially available but can be expensive.

score_rationale: The route is strategically excellent and highly convergent, but relies on some challenging transformations (polyene cyclization, tetrasubstituted alkene dihydroxylation) and uses toxic reagents like OsO4 and SeO2, slightly lowering the feasibility and green scores.
route_score: This route features a highly strategic and elegant biomimetic polyene cyclization to rapidly assemble the complex decalin core. The subsequent steps logically build the remaining rings and append the peripheral groups in a convergent manner. While the key cyclization and some regioselective couplings carry inherent risks, the overall step economy and strategic brilliance make this a very strong synthetic plan.
steer_query: Synthesizing the highly substituted decalin core via a biomimetic Lewis acid-catalyzed polyene cyclization of an acyclic terpene precursor to stereoselectively establish the bicyclic framework.

steps.description: The target molecule can be synthesized via a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling. This simpler strategy disconnects the 4-meth
steps.strategy: The target molecule can be synthesized via a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling. This simpler strategy disconnects the 4-methoxyphenyl ring from the polycyclic core, avoiding the complex biomimetic cascade cyclization. The precursors are 4-methoxyphenylboronic acid and a halogenated or triflated derivative of the intact polycyclic pyrone-terpene core. The reactive components are the boronic acid group on the aryl ring and the leaving group (such as a bromide or triflate) at the substituted position of the pyrone ring. All complex stereocenters within the decalin and pyran rings are fully established in the polycyclic precursor and are completely preserved during this mild, palladium-catalyzed sp2-sp2 coupling.
steps.conditions_as_given: The reaction is run using a transition-metal catalyst (palladium) and a base in a polar solvent mixture at elevated temperature under an inert atmosphere.

steps.description: The corresponding reaction involves an electrophilic aromatic bromination of the unbrominated polycyclic precursor to in
steps.strategy: The corresponding reaction involves an electrophilic aromatic bromination of the unbrominated polycyclic precursor to introduce the bromine atom onto the heterocyclic ring. The strategy focuses on the electron-rich pyrone/phenol-type ring which undergoes regioselective halogenation using a standard brominating agent such as N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) or bromine. This late-stage functionalization approach greatly simplifies the retrosynthesis by leaving the complex, highly functionalized polycyclic terpene framework and all of its established stereocenters completely intact, requiring only the cleavage of the aryl-bromine bond to yield the simpler unbrominated target analog.
steps.conditions_as_given: Electrophilic aromatic bromination using N-bromosuccinimide or bromine in a polar aprotic solvent at ambient temperature.

steps.description: The corresponding reaction involves an intramolecular dehydrative etherification to form the pyran ring, utilizing a pre
steps.strategy: The corresponding reaction involves an intramolecular dehydrative etherification to form the pyran ring, utilizing a precursor that already contains the fully formed decalin framework and the coumarin moiety. The reactive components consist of a free phenolic hydroxyl group on the coumarin ring and a tertiary alcohol on the decalin system. By starting with the intact, stereochemically defined decalin core, this simpler approach avoids complex cascade cyclizations and relies on a straightforward acid-catalyzed ring closure where the rigid geometry of the pre-existing stereocenters dictates the correct formation of the final oxygen heterocycle.
steps.conditions: p-TsOH (cat.), toluene, reflux with Dean-Stark apparatus.
steps.conditions_as_given: The forward reaction is an intramolecular dehydrative etherification typically driven by a Brønsted acid catalyst in an organic solvent at elevated temperature.

steps.description: Osmium tetroxide-mediated cis-dihydroxylation of the tetrasubstituted alkene.
steps.strategy: Osmium tetroxide-mediated cis-dihydroxylation of the tetrasubstituted alkene.
steps.why_critical: Installs the two tertiary alcohols required for the subsequent pyran ring formation, setting up the final cyclization.
steps.main_risk: Poor facial selectivity and low reactivity due to the extreme steric hindrance of the tetrasubstituted alkene.

steps.strategy: Alkylation of the pyrone with an allylic alcohol derived from the decalin core. This can be achieved via Mitsunobu conditions or Lewis acid catalysis.
steps.conditions: BF3·OEt2 or Sc(OTf)3, DCM, 0 °C to rt (to favor C-alkylation over O-alkylation).
steps.why_critical: It joins the two major fragments (the decalin core and the coumarin moiety) via a challenging C-alkylation of a relatively unreactive position.
steps.main_risk: Poor regioselectivity, specifically the competition between O-alkylation and the desired C-alkylation of the 4-hydroxycoumarin.

steps.description: Allylic oxidation of the decalin core using selenium dioxide (SeO2). SeO2 oxidation is highly regioselective for the (E)
steps.strategy: Allylic oxidation of the decalin core using selenium dioxide (SeO2). SeO2 oxidation is highly regioselective for the (E)-methyl group (C14) of the tetrasubstituted double bond due to the steric environment of the decalin framework, avoiding the regioselectivity issues of radical bromination.

steps.description: Biomimetic Lewis acid-catalyzed polyene cyclization. The Lewis acid activates the acyclic ketone precursor, initiating a
steps.strategy: Biomimetic Lewis acid-catalyzed polyene cyclization. The Lewis acid activates the acyclic ketone precursor, initiating a stepwise cationic cascade (Prins-type cyclization followed by alkene addition) that stereoselectively establishes the decalin core and naturally provides the tertiary alcohol at the ring junction.
steps.why_critical: This is the pivotal step of the entire synthesis, rapidly assembling the complex bicyclic decalin core and setting multiple stereocenters in a single cascade operation.
steps.main_risk: Low yield or incorrect relative stereochemistry due to competing elimination pathways or alternative cyclization modes.
